body:
### Summary

### Summary

`uv tool install --force --reinstall <tool>` replaces the tool environment *in place*. A concurrent reader of that environment, such as the running tool itself, or any process importing from its site-packages, observes missing modules and files for the duration of the replacement, while the reinstall exits 0, implying success.

I measured the window with a 10 Hz observer loop: **59 missing samples across ~43 seconds** during a single reinstall of a tool with a few hundred files.

This is the reader-side sibling of #12751 (writer-vs-writer on concurrent `uv sync`). In this bug, for comparison, there there is only one writer, unserialized against readers.

### Repro

Terminal A (observer, 10 Hz):

```bash
while true; do
  ~/.local/share/uv/tools/<tool>/bin/python -c "import <package>" 2>/dev/null \
    || echo "MISSING $(date +%H:%M:%S.%N)"
  sleep 0.1
done
```

Terminal B:

```bash
uv tool install --force --reinstall <tool>
```

Observed: 59 `MISSING` lines spread across ~43 s of the reinstall. Interleaving two reinstalls of the same tool makes the window worse and both still exit 0.

### Expected

Either:

- the replacement is serialized/atomic — build the new environment in a sibling directory and swap (rename or symlink flip), so a reader never observes a partially populated environment  —  or
- the window is documented as expected behavior, so callers know to route unattended reinstalls through a build-then-flip mechanism. (And maybe then add an example of this mechanism.)

### Workaround

I now install tools into an immutable per-version directory and flip a symlink pointer ourselves; the race becomes impossible rather than detectable. The cost is duplicated disk per version and manual reaping.

### Platform

macOS 15.7.3 arm64

### Version

uv 0.12.6 (7938ca5d5 2026-08-25)

### Python version

Python 3.13.15
title: uv tool install --force --reinstall mutates the tool environment in place: concurrent readers observe missing files for tens of seconds while the install exits 0
